master.master_headline: Holding at 8: markets slid a sixth day while Ebola growth eased and talks stayed undated.
master.master_reasoning: This is judgment, not measurement. Same method as before: anchor on the closest civilisation-scale threats, nuclear (4.5) and great-power war (6.5), set the master farther out because those desks' midnights are lower bars than a civilisation-wide point of no return, then pull it back in because one conflict drives several threats at once and correlated risks compound. In twelve hours little changed at the top of the board. The IAEA board met and Iran refused inspectors again, with no resolution reported; the IAEA also flagged North Korea enlarging its enrichment plant; the Shenzhen nuclear-talks pledge still has no date. Those deepen existing risks without crossing anything. The one confirmed move is again the economy: a sixth straight stock loss and a jump in the fear gauge to about 28, with long yields above 5% and a December hike almost fully priced. I move it from 8.3 to 8.0, short of the desk's 7.4, because the 200-day break is unverified and there is still no credit failure. Pulling the other way: Ebola's weekly rise slowed from 510 to 334 cases, a cluster of US outages turned out not to be cyberattacks, and S&P's Hormuz count is flat. The net is close to zero, so the master holds at 8 with a steady trend.

master.where_headed: Next: the COP31 outcome (due to close 20 Nov), any IAEA board resolution, the next weekly Ebola figures to see if the slowdown holds, and whether the Shenzhen dialogue gets a date. After that: comments close on FDA's gene-editing guidance on 27 Nov, Israel's coalition deadline on 6 Dec (extendable), the Fed meeting on 8-9 Dec with a hike nearly fully priced, US inflation data on 10 Dec, and the EU ministers' meeting on 14 Dec where Iran sanctions over the fridge attacks are expected. Over two years the main risks are unchanged: no arms-control successor, AI capability and money running ahead of oversight, and a strong El Nino meeting 2027 harvests while Gulf shipping and fertiliser stay tight.

master.dissent: A reader could argue for 7.5: markets have fallen six days running with the fear gauge near 28, Iran is refusing inspectors and threatening to strike first, North Korea is expanding enrichment, and Ebola is still largely untraced. The case for 8.5 is also there: the three nuclear powers have promised talks, Ebola's weekly growth slowed, the US outage scare was not an attack, oil is steady, credit is calm, and Hormuz crossings are flat by one count.

desks.name: AI Frontier & Safety
desks.midnight_definition: AI systems that can do essentially all cognitive work better, faster and cheaper than humans arrive before society has put effective steering or oversight in place (frontier threshold is the one that matters most).
desks.headline: California sues OpenAI, alleging 80 agent control losses; Google reports exploit tool
desks.summary: The main open items from last edition are now confirmed from primary or specialist sources: California's attorney general filed suit against OpenAI on 16 Nov alleging agent containment failures (allegations, not findings), Google's threat unit reported a hacker-run autonomous exploit framework, and Commerce issued an interim rule on remote access to advanced chips. Anthropic's ANT closed its first day at $97.17 against an $83 IPO price. Oversight is forming through litigation and export rules, not capability limits.

desks.headline: Ebola slows to +334 cases in a week but tops 11,370; H5N1 death in Washington
desks.summary: UKHSA week 46 reports 11,376 confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo) cases and 5,568 deaths in DRC as of 14 Nov, with 334 new cases in the latest report period, down from 510 the week before; contact follow-up remains below target and about two-thirds of deaths are in the community. A Yakima County, Washington resident died of H5N1 on 1 Nov after dairy cattle exposure, the first US bird flu death of 2026, amid 33 infected herds. Treaty pathogen annex still pending (deadline no later than May 2027), US measles status was revoked 17 Nov.

trajectory.two_years: Outcome hinges on whether the PABS annex is agreed and surveillance and vaccination capacity recover. A COVID-scale event remains a tail risk rather than a baseline.

desks.name: Biotech, Longevity & BCI
desks.midnight_definition: The first therapy shown in humans to slow or reverse biological ageing broadly, not just one disease.
desks.headline: FDA drafts one-patient gene-editing pathway; no human ageing endpoint yet
desks.summary: FDA's biologics centre issued draft guidance on 27 Oct 2026 letting bespoke gene-editing products share one licence application; comments close 27 Nov. Beam expects to file the first base-editing BLA (sickle cell) as early as end-2026, while FDA reviews a cancer risk with AAV-vector gene therapies. Melanoma vaccine filing remains unconfirmed and no human clinical ageing endpoint has appeared.

top_stories.title: FDA draft guidance: one licence application for individualised gene-editing products
top_stories.why_it_matters: Would let sponsors cover several patient-specific variants in one BLA and add variants later with lab evidence, easing rare-disease editing; comments due 27 Nov 2026. Narrow-disease, not ageing.

top_stories.title: Beam's risto-cel nears first base-editing BLA; FDA probes AAV cancer risk
top_stories.why_it_matters: Beam expects to submit as early as end-2026 for sickle cell; separately FDA is examining confirmed insertional-oncogenesis cases with Zolgensma and the shared-vector Itvisma, saying benefit still outweighs risk for now.

top_stories.title: Yale-led review of 51 trials: which interventions shift epigenetic age
top_stories.why_it_matters: Largest human check of ageing-clock responsiveness: exercise plus diet, metformin, semaglutide and anti-TNF drugs moved the markers, supplements did not. The outcome was a biomarker, not lifespan or disease, so it does not meet the midnight threshold.

Resolves last edition's date discrepancy in favour of 19 Aug, per trade press dated that day.

trajectory.six_months: FDA decision on Intellia's lonvo-z due 10 March 2027; a melanoma vaccine filing announcement and full INTerpath-001 data are plausible; more rare-disease gene therapy actions. No broad anti-ageing therapy expected.
trajectory.two_years: Personalised vaccines and in vivo editing plausibly approved; ageing trials will probably still report biomarkers or single-disease endpoints until a validated clinical ageing endpoint is accepted.

desks.headline: Nvidia CEO hunt open, no findings yet; Alice & Bob doubles 2030 logical-qubit goal
desks.summary: Nvidia's board is searching internally and externally for a permanent CEO with CFO Kress interim; the Wachtell-led inquiry has published no findings and the DOJ says it has not concluded whether a former Megaspeed executive is a spy. In quantum, Alice & Bob (18 Nov) raised its 2030 target to 200 logical qubits, a vendor roadmap that adds no independent fault-tolerance proof.

desks.name: Climate & Earth Systems
desks.midnight_definition: Crossing self-reinforcing tipping points (ice sheets, AMOC, Amazon, coral reefs, permafrost) that lock in severe warming regardless of later action.
desks.headline: COP31 at its scheduled close with no deal indexed; October 2026 was the warmest on record
desks.summary: COP31 in Antalya is due to end 20 Nov; the latest indexed reporting (to 18 Nov) shows no agreement, a contested 144-paragraph cover decision and a shorter replacement draft promised. Copernicus says October 2026 was the warmest October on record at 1.75C above pre-industrial, with 2026 virtually certain to pass 1.5C, and Nino 3.4 sea temperatures above the peaks of past strong El Ninos. No final COP31 text could be found.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Covers 17 Nov. Island states and the EU-aligned bloc want language on moving away from fossil fuels while the Arab Group rejects top-down roadmaps; the Climate Technology Centre risks losing operating authority after Feb 2027 absent consensus.

top_stories.title: Week two opens split over scope and ambition of cover decision
top_stories.why_it_matters: The draft would triple adaptation finance to at least USD 120bn by 2035 and encourage 35% electrification by 2035; the Arab Group, LMDCs and Russia object to new mandates and the electrification pledge.

top_stories.title: Draft carries two fossil wordings; Bowen says final will differ

desks.headline: US outage cluster has no cyber cause found; EU Iran sanctions on fridge hacks in drafting
desks.summary: A run of US outages on 12-17 Nov (FAA ground stop, Microsoft, AWS, United, JPMorgan, Apple, NSA) has no common cause identified, and officials and companies say none was a cyberattack; the FBI reportedly sees no sign of hacking in the FAA stop. Separately, the EU's top diplomat said new Iran sanctions over the fridge campaign are being drafted, and France says it wants them agreed on 14 Dec. Real cyber incidents this week were ordinary-scale (hospital, university, software supply chain).

The VIX rose to about 28 from about 24.6, while the 10-year stayed near 5.05% and markets priced about a 94% chance of a 25bp December hike per CME. Hot Philadelphia Fed prices-paid and a Fed governor calling for more tightening kept the rate pressure on.

desks.headline: PJM refiled backstop, restart now March 2027; target may shrink below 6.8 GW
desks.summary: PJM filed a revised reliability backstop with FERC on 29 Oct, moving the start to 1 Mar 2027 with results due 10 May, after FERC rejected most of the original plan in late September. On fusion, no net-energy result; SPARC and Helion still target 2027 and 2028 on the latest dated reports I saw.

desks.headline: Shenzhen nuclear-risk pledge has no date; Iran deadlock and Ukraine grid war go on
desks.summary: The first three-way Xi-Trump-Putin meeting took place in Shenzhen on 19 November (about 70 minutes) and produced a joint declaration that nuclear war must never be fought and a pledge to start a dialogue on nuclear risk, with no timetable, format or treaty. No breakthrough was announced on Iran or Ukraine. In the Gulf, Iran warned on 16 November it might strike first before another US attack as a US carrier arrived, and the Hormuz disruption and the reported US blockade persist (background re-read 12 Nov; not re-verified for 20 Nov).

top_stories.title: Trump, Xi, Putin pledge nuclear dialogue after Shenzhen summit

desks.midnight_definition: A breakdown of the shared ability to govern and to agree on facts, such that large societies can no longer correct their own mistakes.
desks.headline: Israel's Eisenkot bloc still short of 61 as Bennett-Netanyahu meeting stirs talks
desks.summary: Rule-of-law indices still point down while the EIU shows a small uptick. In Israel, the Eisenkot-led bloc holds 48 of 120 seats and is courting a Haredi party (55 with UTJ), with a mandate of 28 days extendable by 14; a Bennett-Netanyahu security briefing on 18 Nov added uncertainty. Brazil's electoral court has admitted, not decided, abuse-of-power complaints against the winning ticket.

top_stories.title: Israel: Bennett meets Netanyahu as Eisenkot bloc meets; rotation idea rejected
top_stories.why_it_matters: Reports say Bennett proposed a rotation government, which the Eisenkot camp rejected; his side says he will not serve under Netanyahu. The bloc has 48 seats, the Netanyahu bloc 53, and the Joint List and Ra'am (19 together) could be decisive.

top_stories.title: Israel: Eisenkot courts UTJ for a 55-seat minority government; conscription is the sticking point
top_stories.why_it_matters: Even with UTJ the plan is six seats short of 61. The Haredi side wants deferment for Torah students and an override clause; no framework is agreed, and Liberman opposes relying on Ra'am.

top_stories.title: Knesset elects Eisenkot ally as speaker, 66 to 52
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows the bloc plus allies can win floor votes and now sets which bills advance, including a judicial committee and an inquiry into 7 October. Likud condemned the vote; Netanyahu remains caretaker.

top_stories.title: Brazil: electoral court admits Novo party complaint against Lula and Alckmin
top_stories.why_it_matters: The complaint seeks revocation of the ticket's diplomas and eight-year ineligibility. The reporting judge found it can proceed but did not assess wrongdoing; the defence has five days to respond and no timetable is given.

desks.name: Nuclear & Strategic Weapons
desks.midnight_definition: The first use of a nuclear weapon in war, or an uncontrolled escalation toward large-scale nuclear exchange, which cannot be undone.
desks.headline: West presses Iran at IAEA board; IAEA flags North Korea enrichment expansion
desks.summary: No treaty caps US and Russian strategic arsenals since New START lapsed in February 2026, and the Doomsday Clock stands at a record 85 seconds. The IAEA board opened its quarterly meeting on 18 November: the US, UK, France and Germany pressed Iran to readmit inspectors, Iran refused citing threats of fresh attack, and no resolution had been reported by 19 November. The IAEA also reported an extension to North Korea's Yongbyon enrichment plant.

top_stories.title: West presses Iran at IAEA board to readmit inspectors; Iran refuses
top_stories.why_it_matters: Four Western states say the IAEA has lost track of Iran's verified enriched uranium for about a year and a half; Iran ties access to an end of threats. No resolution or vote reported yet.

top_stories.title: IAEA: North Korea extending Yongbyon enrichment plant
top_stories.why_it_matters: Grossi told the board the extension's exterior was finished by late October and enrichment runs at Kangson and Yongbyon; fissile material output is growing with no inspector access since 2009.

top_stories.title: Iran security chief: no enriched material will leave the country
top_stories.why_it_matters: Rezaei also warned of consequences for new US strikes, hardening Tehran's position as the IAEA board meets and shutting off a stockpile-removal deal.

top_stories.title: Iran calls IAEA board resolutions flawed, rules out normal inspections
top_stories.why_it_matters: Iran's Vienna mission says normal safeguards cannot resume after attacks on its facilities and faults Grossi's reports; access deadlock persists.

top_stories.title: IAEA says Iran's highly enriched uranium still unaccounted for; board meets next
top_stories.why_it_matters: Inspectors have been shut out since the June 2025 strikes and cannot say where about 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium is; Iran rules out regular monitoring for now.

top_stories.title: IAEA voices growing concern over Iran's underground enrichment plant

trajectory.two_years: Without a successor framework, warhead uploads and a three-way US-Russia-China build-up become the default. Iran's nuclear choice and the testing moratorium are the main wildcards.

desks.name: Food, Water & Resources
desks.midnight_definition: Simultaneous failure of several major food-producing regions, or a resource shock, that causes mass hunger across multiple continents.
desks.headline: El Niño drought deepens Sudan famine; Egypt fertiliser gas cuts and Hormuz strain persist
desks.summary: NOAA's 12 Nov update (via local news) puts the Nino-3.4 anomaly near +2.5C with high odds of a very strong event into early 2027, and the Oct 12 IPC Sudan report ties El Niño drought to crop failure across Darfur and Kordofan, with 135,000 people in IPC Phase 5. Egypt's fertiliser gas cuts (Mopco 33%, Kima 20%) have no end date and urea is near $535/t. Hormuz traffic is reduced but not stalled by two different counts; headline food prices remain moderate and no multi-continent failure is visible yet.

top_stories.title: NOAA 12 Nov: El Niño near +2.5C, over 79% odds strong into early 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: A strong event is expected to keep building into winter and weaken in early 2027, with about 60% odds of record strength. This raises 2027 yield risk in Southern Hemisphere and Asian crop regions; next update is 10 Dec.

top_stories.title: IPC: 19.5 million in acute hunger in Sudan, famine in parts of Darfur
top_stories.why_it_matters: 135,000 people were in Phase 5 (assessment data from May), with famine-level malnutrition in two South Darfur camps and El Niño drought hitting crops across more than half the country. It is the clearest case of El Niño plus war plus aid gaps already causing hunger.

top_stories.title: Egypt fertiliser gas cut reaches 33% at Mopco; plant reports conflict
top_stories.why_it_matters: The 33% cut took effect 8 Nov after 20% from 1 Nov, with no end date. Abu Qir is reported at 33% by one outlet and 20% by another, and Kima has only confirmed 20%. Granular urea is about $535/t FOB.

top_stories.title: Hormuz crossings at 750 in October, a three-month high, despite attacks
top_stories.why_it_matters: S&P counted 750 transits (749 in September), with LNG carriers at 32, the most since the conflict began, but crude VLCCs fell to 156 from 184. Red Sea Bab al-Mandab transits rose to 1,196. This is a different measure from UKMTO's 65% below pre-war figure last edition.

top_stories.title: Hormuz weekly transits slipped to 116, crude voyages down about 12%
top_stories.why_it_matters: Lloyd's List Intelligence counts non-Iranian-linked cargo transits at 116 for 19-25 Oct (124 prior week), a three-week average of 121 versus 132 earlier; traffic is slowed, not collapsed. Another measure alongside UKMTO and S&P.

top_stories.title: UKMTO: Hormuz transits about 65% below pre-war, 11 ships hit in a week
top_stories.why_it_matters: UKMTO counted 170 outbound and 155 inbound transits and JMIC held the threat at severe. Oil, LNG and fertiliser freight stay exposed.

trajectory.six_months: Fertiliser costs and a peaking-then-fading very strong El Niño shape 2027 planting and early harvests; Sudan and other hotspots stay at famine risk without more aid.
trajectory.two_years: If Hormuz stays impaired and a record El Niño cuts yields in several regions, a multi-continent food price spike is plausible; if shipping normalises the system probably absorbs it with rising regional hunger.

signals_to_watch: NOAA CPC ENSO update 2026-12-10 and Australian, Indian, Brazilian crop estimates

Offsetting forces leave the clock at 6.0; someone could move it closer by weighting a record El Niño plus fertiliser tightness, or farther on Hormuz recovery.

desks.name: Robotics & Autonomy
desks.midnight_definition: General-purpose robots (humanoid or otherwise) doing ordinary physical work at scale more cheaply than human labour, across many job types rather than in a few controlled niches.
desks.headline: Autonomy spreads city by city; Tesla scale deferred, humanoids still unproven
desks.summary: Narrow autonomy keeps scaling: Baidu's Apollo Go reached 30 cities by October and Tesla opened unsupervised robotaxis in San Antonio on 9 Nov, but independent trackers showed only tens of unsupervised Tesla cars in April and Musk deferred large scale to a software overhaul due late 2026 to early 2027. Tesla's Q3 update floated 20,000 Optimus robots a week by 2027 while admitting the robot struggles with varied tasks, so humanoid claims remain far ahead of delivered work.

top_stories.title: Baidu Q3: Apollo Go in 30 cities, 34 million autonomous km in the quarter
top_stories.why_it_matters: The largest non-US robotaxi operator keeps widening its footprint, doubling its Dubai fleet (on Uber) and testing in London; the article gives no ride counts, so volume is unconfirmed.

top_stories.title: Musk says Optimus could reach 20,000 a week by 2027; robot still fails varied tasks
top_stories.why_it_matters: Tesla's Q3 update says Fremont Optimus lines are running, but the target is conditional on more engineering and Musk concedes weak autonomy on varied tasks; Unitree's founder spoke of self-improving robots cleaning rooms as early as next year.

top_stories.title: Tesla unsupervised fleet was 25 cars per tracker; Musk defers scale to FSD v15
top_stories.why_it_matters: Closes the fleet-size thread only partly: Tesla publishes no count, a community tracker found 25 unsupervised cars in Texas in April, and Musk said large-scale deployment waits for FSD v15 (late 2026 to early 2027) with no material revenue before 2027. desks.name: Global Health & Demographics
desks.midnight_definition: Demographic and social strain (ageing, shrinking workforces, health-funding collapse) becomes so severe that major societies can no longer sustain their pensions, health systems and workforce.
desks.headline: Global health aid to hit $42.6B in 2026, lowest since 2012; US measles at 5,412
desks.summary: IHME estimates development assistance for health falls to $42.6 billion in 2026, down 5% on 2025 after a 12% drop in 2024, with US cuts of 45% since 2024. US measles reached 5,412 cases (CDC data to 12 Nov), up 230 in a week, with six CDC-listed deaths. Against this, WHO says global life expectancy has nearly recovered to its pre-pandemic level (73.3 vs 73.4 years).

top_stories.title: Global health aid set to fall to $42.6B in 2026, lowest since 2012
top_stories.why_it_matters: IHME estimates a 5% fall after 12% in 2024; US health aid is down about $5.9B (45%) since 2024, the UK 37%. Deepens the financing squeeze on HIV, TB and immunisation in poorer countries.
top_stories.source_name: Ghana News Agency via GhanaWeb (citing IHME)

top_stories.title: US measles rises to 5,412 cases, up 230 in a week
top_stories.why_it_matters: CDC data as of 12 Nov: 43 outbreaks, 6 deaths listed, 47 jurisdictions; about 96% of cases are outbreak-linked. Shows continued spread amid weakened vaccination coverage. Al Jazeera reported on 7 Nov that 2026 passed 5,000 cases, the highest in 35 years.

top_stories.title: CDC confirms 6 measles deaths in 2026 (state tallies differ)
top_stories.why_it_matters: Headline seen in search only; page not fetchable. Death count dispute with state tallies unresolved.

top_stories.title: WHO: life expectancy 73.3 years, nearly back to pre-pandemic
top_stories.why_it_matters: Healthy life expectancy (62.8) is still 0.4 years below 2019; noncommunicable diseases cause 74% of deaths and dementia is now the fifth leading cause, which raises long-term care and pension burdens.

top_stories.title: UNAIDS: international HIV funding fell 18% in 2025, resurgence risk
top_stories.why_it_matters: Donor HIV money dropped from $8.8B to $7.3B; about 1.2 million new infections and 570,000 AIDS deaths in 2025, with infections rising in 21 countries. Without faster action UNAIDS projects over 3 million extra infections by 2030.

top_stories.title: Zero-dose children fall to 13.5 million in 2025, still above 2019
top_stories.why_it_matters: WHO/UNICEF estimates show a slight improvement over 2024 but 74 countries are worse than in 2019. Measles coverage has not recovered, with 1.8 million more unprotected children than in 2019.

top_stories.title: South Korea births up 13% in August, 26th straight monthly rise
top_stories.why_it_matters: About 23,700 births in August; January-August up 14.5%. Still far below replacement, but decline is not uniform.

trajectory.six_months: Expect more US measles cases and first hard data on HIV, TB and malaria programme disruption as Global Fund 2026-2028 allocations take effect; East Asian birth data for early 2027.
trajectory.two_years: Further donor retrenchment would likely reverse immunisation and HIV gains in fragile settings, while ageing keeps forcing pension fights in Europe and Asia.

desks.clock_reasoning: Demographic decline is near-certain but pension and health-system failure is gradual and policy-dependent, so the 10 to 20 band fits. Newly estimated aid at its lowest since 2012 and rising US measles are real stresses, but WHO shows life expectancy nearly recovered and no measured system collapse. Someone expecting faster damage from aid cuts would set it lower; this is judgment, not measurement.

desks.name: Space
desks.midnight_definition: Permanent human presence beyond Earth becomes self-sustaining in practice: routine, cheap, fully reusable heavy lift plus a crewed base that persists.
desks.headline: Starship ship caught from orbit; booster lost; Flight 16 still undated
desks.summary: Flight 15 (13 Nov) put 26 Starlink V3 satellites in orbit and the ship was reported caught by the tower on 14 Nov, a first, while the booster catch was aborted and it was lost in the Gulf. No FAA finding, Flight 16 date, Mengzhou 1 or Blue Moon MK1 launch was found this run. NASA plans Artemis III docking tests with both landers in summer 2027 and a landing as early as 2028.

top_stories.why_it_matters: First orbital-ship catch is a key step to full reuse; the lost booster shows both-stage reuse is unproven.

top_stories.title: Flight 15 launches 22-hour test; booster catch aborted
top_stories.why_it_matters: Confirms launch time, Starlink V3 deployment and the aborted booster catch; cause not stated.

top_stories.why_it_matters: SpaceX plans Florida Starship launches within months; NASA says Artemis III docking tests in summer 2027, landing possibly 2028.

trajectory.two_years: Artemis III orbital rehearsal in 2027 and a landing attempt around Artemis IV in 2028 are the milestones; a persistent crewed base is still beyond this window.

desks.name: Natural Hazards & Wildcards
desks.midnight_definition: A natural or out-of-the-blue event (supervolcanic eruption, impactor, extreme solar storm, mega-quake) with global consequences that nobody was positioned for.
desks.headline: Kilauea episode 57 due 18-22 Nov; Banda Sea quake and sun stay regional
desks.summary: Hazards remain regional. USGS expects Kilauea's 57th fountaining episode between 18 and 22 Nov (as of its 15 Nov update), with the summit still reinflating and no start confirmed in anything I could read. The 16 Nov Banda Sea quake (BMKG 6.8, USGS-based listing 6.6) carried no tsunami potential. The newest solar report I could read (16 Nov) showed low X-flare odds and at most minor geomagnetic storms.

top_stories.title: Kilauea: episode 57 forecast for 18-22 Nov as summit reinflates
top_stories.why_it_matters: The forecast window has slid later three times as inflation slowed; hazards stay inside Halemaumau crater (ash, gas, tephra), with alert level Advisory.

top_stories.title: Banda Sea quake: BMKG says 6.8, no tsunami potential, no damage reported

trajectory.two_years: Solar flare intensity should decline though extreme storms stay possible; Campi Flegrei unrest could plateau or escalate; Iceland's Reykjanes system is likely to erupt again with regional effect.
